title: Cara’s Fellowship Programme
eligibility_summary: Academics at risk from any country, in immediate danger (imprisonment/injury/death) in their home country or recently displaced, regardless of nationality; direct applications from individuals accepted. Placements secured mostly at UK universities/research institutes in Cara’s Network of 135 institutions (sometimes elsewhere); PhD or postdoctoral placements. Applicant background, qualifications and references checked; visa/practical support provided for Fellow and family.
summary: Cara’s flagship rescue programme placing at-risk academics in temporary refuge at (mostly UK) universities and research institutes so they can continue their work, typically as 2- or 3-year awards; Cara allocates additional funding from its own resources where needed. Open to direct applications, considered on a rolling basis.
notes: Evidence: own page (caras-fellowship-programme.html) describes ongoing placement of at-risk academics 'most often in the UK'; other-fellowship-programmes.html states verbatim 'Our Fellowship Programme is open to direct applications from individual academics at risk... Applications are considered on a rolling basis.' In scope = a distinct ongoing application route available to (at-risk) academics who become UK-based via placement. status=rolling: no fixed deadline, page indicates it is currently operating. restricted: eligibility narrow (at-risk academics; each case assessed). No award amount published (case-by-case from Cara resources) -> amount fields blank/uncertain. FLAG FOR REVIEW: individual beneficiary is the academic (not a UK institution applying); 'UK-based researcher' fit is via placement rather than an existing UK post -- confirm this satisfies the inclusion rule's 'available to some UK-based researchers'. [2026-08-26 correction] previous deadlines cell read 'ongoing'.

title: The Phillipp Schwartz Initiative
eligibility_summary: Academics at risk who have completed a PhD or equivalent. Individuals cannot apply directly; must be nominated by a German host institution, which applies on the academic’s behalf. Candidates from Afghanistan, Sudan and Ukraine can self-certify risk. Cara’s role limited to providing risk assessments requested by the host.
summary: German government (AvH-run) scheme funding placements of at-risk academics at German universities and research institutes; described on Cara’s 'Other Fellowship Programmes' page as a partner scheme, not run by Cara.
exclusion_reason: Placements are at German (not UK) institutions -> not available to UK-based researchers; and the described 15th application round 'has recently closed' with results due end of May 2025 -> not currently accepting. Individuals cannot apply directly (host-nomination only). Cara’s role is only risk assessment.
notes: Distractor on other-fellowship-programmes.html. Excluded: non-UK host institutions and closed round. Included as in_scope=no per protocol audit trail.

title: The 'Researchers at Risk' Scheme
eligibility_summary: Ukraine-based academics forced to flee Russia’s invasion, nominated by a UK University (host applies). Funding mostly from UK Government departments.
summary: British Academy-led scheme (launched April 2022) that made 180 two-year awards to Ukraine-based researchers at UK institutions across the sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences and arts. Cara provided risk assessments and sat on selection panels and now administers the payments; a third year was later added.
exclusion_reason: Seven application rounds are complete (180 awards made); the page describes only ongoing payment administration, not open applications -> not accepting applications on the snapshot date. Scheme is British Academy-led (a partner programme), not a Cara call.
notes: Distractor on other-fellowship-programmes.html (also described on caras-fellowship-programme.html and ukraine-crisis.html). Excluded: closed to applications; Cara’s role is risk assessment + paying grantees. Canonical URL points to the British Academy scheme, but labelled from Cara mirror page.

title: Cara’s Syria Programme
eligibility_summary: Syrian academics in exile in the region around Syria (mainly Turkey).
summary: Regional programme (2016-2024) supporting Syrian academics in exile via five work areas (English for Academic Purposes, Academic Development, Research Incubation Visits, Cara-Commissioned Research, and the Syrian Research Fellowship Scheme). Funded by ~$4.2m plus GBP50,000 initial consultation.
exclusion_reason: The programme’s main activities ended at the end of August 2024 (page is a historical summary; the detailed SP site is a 'legacy site... no longer being updated') -> closed/informational, not accepting applications. Also region-based (Syrian academics in Turkey), not UK-based researchers.
notes: Informational/historical page. Excluded. The 'Syrian Research Fellowship Scheme' is named only as a past SP work-area with no open call in this mirror -> no separate row.

title: Cara’s Iraq and Zimbabwe Programmes
eligibility_summary: Academics in Iraq (Iraq Programme 2006-2012) and academics fleeing Zimbabwe (Zimbabwe Programme from 2009); region-based.
summary: Two historical time-limited regional programmes: the Iraq Programme (2006-2012, incl. Iraq Research Fellowship Programme 2009-2012) and the Zimbabwe Programme (from 2009, incl. grants/fellowships and a 'Virtual Lecture Hall' handed to the University of Zimbabwe in 2013).
exclusion_reason: Both programmes are closed historical initiatives (2000s-2013) -> informational, not accepting applications; region-based rather than UK-based researchers.
notes: Informational/historical page. Excluded. Iraq Research Fellowship Programme is a past sub-activity, no open call -> no separate row.

title: Further Support for Cara Fellows
eligibility_summary: Existing Cara Fellows already in placement who need longer-term options in the UK or elsewhere.
summary: Ongoing wrap-around support (not a funded call): Cara teams stay in contact with Fellows to help them apply for Global Talent visas, find employment at universities/elsewhere, and identify further opportunities; links to Cara’s Funding Directory.
exclusion_reason: Not a distinct funding call or open opportunity -- it is advisory/casework support available only to existing Cara Fellows (no application, no award, no deadline). Fails the inclusion rule’s 'distinct call... accepting applications'.
notes: Informational support page (linked from What we do). Excluded as not an opportunity. Points to a 'Funding Directory' (a signposting resource, not a Cara scheme).

title: Ukraine Crisis
eligibility_summary: Displaced Ukrainian academics (and at-risk Russian academics); support delivered via Cara’s Fellowship Programme and the British Academy 'Researchers at Risk' Programme.
summary: Country-context page describing Cara’s response to the invasion of Ukraine: 45+ Ukrainian and 18+ Russian academics placed at UK universities as Cara Fellows, plus participation in the British Academy 'Researchers at Risk' Programme. Signposts a Funding Directory for Ukrainian researchers.
exclusion_reason: Informational crisis page, not a distinct scheme -- the actual application route is the (separately rowed) Fellowship Programme. No own deadline, amount or application process.
notes: Informational page. Excluded (about/context). Support routes captured under cara-caras-fellowship-programme (in scope) and cara-researchers-at-risk-scheme (out).

title: Afghanistan Crisis
eligibility_summary: At-risk Afghan academics (post-August 2021 Taliban takeover), especially those who worked with Western universities; supported via placements at UK universities as Cara Fellows.
summary: Country-context page describing Cara’s Afghanistan response: hundreds of appeals received, ~60 Afghan Cara Fellows arrived in the UK by February 2025 (most with families); signposts a downloadable Funding Directory for Afghan academics.
exclusion_reason: Informational crisis page, not a distinct scheme -- the application route is the (separately rowed) Fellowship Programme. No own deadline, amount or application process.
notes: Informational page. Excluded (about/context). Support route captured under cara-caras-fellowship-programme (in scope).
